definition_title: Lengths of prime-factor quotients after localization
natural_language_statement: Let R be a commutative ring, let Q be a prime ideal minimal over I, and let P be a prime ideal containing I. After localization at Q, the module length of the quotient by the image of P is 1 when P = Q and 0 when P ≠ Q. The exported supporting results show that an ideal P not contained in Q maps to the unit ideal, that the corresponding quotient has length zero, and that the quotient by the localized maximal ideal has length one.
explanation: If P differs from the minimal prime Q while containing I, minimality rules out P ≤ Q; an element of P outside Q becomes a unit after localization, so the localized ideal is top and its quotient has length zero. In the equal-prime case the quotient is the residue field of the local ring and has length one. The combined theorem packages these two cases.
